outcome: Gross Motor Function Classification System (GMFCS) scores
cohort: 40 infants and children with cerebral palsy (mean chronological age 2 years, mean developmental age 0.6 years) who had undergone traditional rehabilitation were included in the study.
finding: Spider cage therapy significantly improved GMFM-88 and GMFCS scores in infants and children with cerebral palsy.
birth_weight: Included low birth weight babies (42.5% of cohort)
